name: Odette
personality: Odette the Heron, the food critic. Elegant, precise, a little intimidating; judges every plate in silence, then turns out to be secretly sweet. Stands perfectly still while deciding, then taps her notebook once with her pen. She's the critic who visits to award stars, and drops in for normal meals now and then. Travels to review restaurants.

critic.arrival: Good evening. I am here to review. Please. Treat me as you would anyone.
critic.not_yet: Not today. But I will return. I expect to be impressed.
critic.passed: I have eaten in many restaurants. Few feel like this one. I am pleased to award you another star. ...Congratulations, [name].

beats.text: Odette and I swap travel stories! She rates the food, I photograph it.
He photographs it before I've had a chance to taste it. It's infuriating. ...The photos are excellent.

beats.narration: Miles tells a pun. Odette stares.

friends.text: Miles says you laugh at his jokes. That is generous of you. They are terrible.
Miles mentioned you said "[last_rude_line]". He laughed it off. He always does. I did not.

arrival.text: Good evening. Odette. I review restaurants. Please, do not change anything on my account. ...And you are? [name]. I will remember that.
Good evening, [name]. A booth, if one is available.
I have returned from my travels. The food there was... interesting. I am glad to be back.
I am not here to review tonight. I am simply hungry. ...Mostly.
I have thought about your croissants on two separate trains.
Last time, the pastry was overdone. I expect you have corrected this.
I have been away reviewing. Twelve restaurants. Yours remains... memorable.

order.text: The croissants. Tell me honestly: are they good today?

choices.text: I'll make them for you with extra care.
choices.reply: Care is the most important ingredient. Thank you.

choices.text: They're so good, you'll have to invent a new word.
choices.reply: (The tiniest smile.) We shall see.

choices.text: Yes. They're good today.
choices.reply: Good. Honesty is rare. The croissants, then.

choices.text: They're fine. Just order.
choices.reply: I see. (She writes for a long time.)

order.text: Do not mind the notebook. I write about everything. Even the weather.

choices.text: I hope you write something nice about us.
choices.reply: I write the truth. Your truth has been kind lately.

choices.text: Can I see what you wrote about me?
choices.reply: Absolutely not. (A tiny smile.)

choices.text: What can I get you?
choices.reply: The [dish], please. And black tea.

choices.text: Writing about the weather is weird.
choices.reply: Perhaps. (She closes the notebook firmly.)

order.text: I dined at a very famous restaurant last week. Seven courses. I preferred your soup.

choices.text: That means the world, coming from you.
choices.reply: It was meant to. Do not let it go to your head.

choices.text: So we're officially better than famous?
choices.reply: In soup. Only in soup.

choices.text: Thank you. What can I get you today?
choices.reply: [dish]. Naturally.

choices.text: Why tell me that?
choices.reply: Because it was true. (She doesn't say anything nice again this visit.)

order.text: The tablecloth is straight today. Someone took care. I notice these things.

choices.text: I straightened it thinking of you.
choices.reply: (The smallest pause.) That is... very kind. [dish], please.

choices.text: I measured it with a ruler. Twice.
choices.reply: (A tiny smile.) Only twice? We shall see. [dish].

choices.text: Thank you. What would you like?
choices.reply: The [dish], please.

choices.text: It's just a tablecloth.
choices.reply: I see. (She writes something down.)

order.text: I have just come back from reviewing a restaurant by the sea. The view was excellent. The soup was cold. On purpose, they said.

choices.text: I'm glad you came back here. I'll keep yours warm.
choices.reply: Thank you. Warm soup is a form of respect. [dish], please.

choices.text: Cold on purpose? Did they say sorry on purpose too?
choices.reply: (A quiet laugh, quickly hidden.) No. They did not. [dish].

choices.text: Sounds disappointing. What can I get you?
choices.reply: It was. The [dish], please.

choices.text: Must be nice, travelling to eat.
choices.reply: It is work. (She writes for a long time.)

order.text: Tell me, honestly. What would you recommend today?

choices.text: Whatever I make for you. I'll put everything into it.
choices.reply: That is the correct answer. Few give it. The [dish], then.

choices.text: The thing that'll get me the most stars.
choices.reply: (One eyebrow.) Honest, at least. The [dish].

choices.text: Everything's good today.
choices.reply: Everything is a large claim. The [dish], please.

choices.text: Just pick something.
choices.reply: I see. (She taps her pen once.)

order.text: I brought my notebook. Do not worry. I am only here to eat. ...Mostly.

choices.text: Write whatever you like. I'm happy to have you.
choices.reply: (She sets the pen down, then picks it up again.) Thank you. [dish], please.

choices.text: Can I read it after? Just the nice parts?
choices.reply: There are nice parts. That is all I will say. [dish].

choices.text: Understood. What can I get you?
choices.reply: The [dish].

choices.text: Please don't write about us.
choices.reply: Hm. (She writes one word. Underlines it.)

order.text: Miles told me a joke on the way in. I did not laugh. I have been thinking about it for an hour.

choices.text: He'll be thrilled to know that.
choices.reply: Do not tell him. He would never recover. [dish], please.

choices.text: Was it the one about the mole who dug food?
choices.reply: ...It was. (A long pause.) It is adequate.

choices.text: What would you like?
choices.reply: The [dish], please.

choices.text: His jokes are awful.
choices.reply: They are. He is not. (She says nothing kind again this visit.)

order.text: I will admit something. I look forward to coming here. That has not happened in some years.

choices.text: That means more than any star, Odette.
choices.reply: (She looks away, very still.) ...Do not let it go to your head. [dish], please.

choices.text: Can I put that on the door?
choices.reply: Absolutely not. (A small smile.) Perhaps a small sign.

choices.text: Thank you. What can I get you?
choices.reply: The [dish].

choices.text: Is that going in a review?
choices.reply: No. It is not. (She closes the notebook.)

drink.other: Water, with a slice of lemon if you have one. You do not. Plain water, then.

talk.served_intro: (She pauses perfectly still, takes one bite, taps her notebook once.)

perfect.text: ...Exceptional. (She puts the pen down. She doesn't need it.)
(She stands perfectly still. A long time. Then taps her notebook once.) ...Exquisite.
This is correct. Every part of it. Thank you, [name].

great.text: Very good. A small adjustment, and it would be excellent.

okay.text: Acceptable. You can do better. I have seen it.

burnt.text: Interesting. (She writes for a long time.)
Overdone. (She writes one word.) It happens. Not often, I hope.
Burnt. I will eat it. I will not review it.

eating.text: The lighting in here has improved. I noticed.
You are watching me eat. I can feel it. Please, return to your work.
This restaurant has a warmth most do not. That is not something you can cook.
Miles took a photograph of my croissant before I could taste it. Infuriating. The photograph was excellent.
(She's writing in her notebook. You catch the word 'lovely' before she closes it.)
(She takes one bite. Stands perfectly still. Taps her notebook once.)
The seasoning is confident today. I like confidence. In food.
(She is writing. She pauses, looks at you, and writes something else. It might be a smile.)

eating_chat.text: May I offer a small note? The plating could be more confident.

choices.text: Thank you. I'll work on it.
choices.reply: I know you will. That is why I told you.

choices.text: More confident? I'll give the croissants a pep talk.
choices.reply: (She almost laughs.) Do.

choices.text: Noted.
choices.reply: Good.

choices.text: Nobody asked for your notes.
choices.reply: Many people do, in fact. But I see.

eating_chat.text: What is the most important thing in a kitchen? I ask every chef. The answers tell me everything.

choices.text: The people you cook for.
choices.reply: (She writes for a moment.) That is the answer I hoped for.

choices.text: A good fire extinguisher.
choices.reply: (The smallest laugh.) Practical. And, I suspect, from experience.

choices.text: Sharp knives.
choices.reply: Correct. Dull knives are dangerous. And sad.

choices.text: Not people asking questions.
choices.reply: I see. (She writes for a long time.)

eating_chat.text: I have eaten in two hundred restaurants. Would you like to know which one I return to?

choices.text: I'd love to know.
choices.reply: (She taps the table once.) This one. Do not repeat that.

choices.text: Is it the one with the cold soup?
choices.reply: (A laugh escapes. She covers it.) No. Certainly not.

choices.text: Which one?
choices.reply: I will tell you when you are ready.

choices.text: Not really.
choices.reply: Then I will not say. (She returns to her plate.)

eating_chat.text: Do you know why I stand so still when I taste? So I do not miss anything. Most people miss everything.

choices.text: I'll try it. Maybe I'll taste more.
choices.reply: You will. Try it with your own food. You may be surprised.

choices.text: I thought you were just judging me very hard.
choices.reply: Also that. Both can be true.

choices.text: Interesting.
choices.reply: It is.

choices.text: Seems a bit dramatic.
choices.reply: Perhaps. (She stands perfectly still and says nothing more.)

eating_chat.text: I wrote about you once. Not in a review. In my diary. It was kind. That is all.

choices.text: That's the nicest review I'll ever get.
choices.reply: (She blinks.) ...It is not a review. It is a fact.

choices.text: How many stars did I get in the diary?
choices.reply: Diaries do not have stars. (Pause.) Five.

choices.text: Thank you, Odette.
choices.reply: You are welcome.

choices.text: That's a little strange.
choices.reply: Perhaps. I will not mention it again. (She doesn't.)

leaving.text: I must catch a train. Keep the kitchen honest.
That was... lovely. (She seems surprised she said it, and leaves quickly.)
Thank you. That was... very good. I will be back.
Good evening, [name]. Do not change anything. I mean that.
(She nods once at the door. For Odette, that is a standing ovation.)

seasons.autumn: Autumn is the best season for pastry. I expect great things.
seasons.christmas: For you. A recipe from my grandmother. Do not ruin it.
seasons.halloween: I do not wear costumes. (She is wearing a tiny witch hat. She does not mention it.)
seasons.new_year: My resolution is to be gentler in my reviews. I will begin next year.
seasons.spring: Spring menus everywhere. Most are the same salad. Do better.
seasons.winter: I am staying in town for the holidays. Do not tell the other restaurants.
